note: Narration v3: the v2 lines rewritten for speech (D-93). Same line numbers and start times as src/scenes/voice-v2.json; figures unchanged. Eric's own opening lines (eric.wav) are not part of this file.

lines.4: A building shows up as a stack of flat drawings. The mistakes hide between the floors.
lines.5: One sheet covers four floors. The bill priced just one. Landsight finds the other three.
lines.6: The roof has thirty centimetres of soil. The rule says forty.
lines.7: Two sheets? Same drawing, different titles.
lines.8: A planter on the lift shaft? That goes back.
lines.9: Here, planters squeeze the escape corridor down to ninety centimetres. The code wants one-twenty.
lines.10: On the ground, a row of trees.
lines.11: You see a tree. A computer just sees twelve loose lines.
lines.12: Muse Spark sees one tree, then asks you before it counts.
lines.13: Just a coloured picture? SAM 3.1 measures every patch. The lawn's a hundred and ninety-five square metres. The drawings say two hundred.
lines.14: The bill says twelve. Eight are drawn.
lines.15: One hedge label means a hundred and eighty-two plants. The bill's in metres.
lines.16: The pavers? Ten thousand over your price list.
lines.17: On the slab, the pits are too small. So big trees count as small, and the greenery falls short. Seven more trees fix it.
lines.18: A developer told us: send the nonsense straight back, and flag the rest one by one.
lines.19: Drop in the folder, as is. Every file gets a verdict, and it names the bill that counts.
lines.20: It reads the project straight off the title block. Your price list, your local rules. Hit analyze.
lines.21: Muse Spark reads every sheet. SAM 3.1 measures the colour plans. Geometry counts. All in about two minutes.
lines.22: On the right, it's sorted the way developers work: send back, fix before pricing, the code. Every item opens on the drawing, and nothing counts until you confirm.
lines.23: Short on greenery? It shows you the fixes that would pass.
lines.24: Pick what goes back. It writes the change request, clouded and priced right on the drawing, and drafts your reply to the developer, ready to send.
lines.25: Point at anything and ask. It answers from the package, and it'll tell you when you're wrong.
lines.26: We planted thirty errors. It found twenty-eight, flagged two, missed none.
lines.27: Every number, traced to the drawing.
